summary.text: A 19-year-old male born late preterm at 36 + 5 weeks had multiple congenital abnormalities (left thumb polydactyly, webbed neck, facial dysmorphism, patent ductus arteriosus and a left ectopic kidney). He had surgical PDA ligation without complications, neurodevelopmental delay with intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, repeated childhood admissions for bronchopulmonary infection, mild AST and ALP increases from age 3, and pruritus after age 13.

In 2022 he was brought in for elevated liver enzymes found at health checkups; he was anicteric with enlarged liver and spleen, and sonography suggested cirrhosis. Virology and autoimmune immunoblot serology were negative, IgG was slightly elevated, urinary and serum copper and serum manganese were increased, and MRCP, CT, endoscopy and brain MRI were performed. A liver biopsy showed advanced cirrhosis, ductopenia, copper deposition and interface hepatitis.

Stage IV primary biliary cholangitis with features of autoimmune hepatitis was diagnosed, Wilson disease was ruled out, and whole exome sequencing found no pathogenic variants for hereditary cholestatic disorders. Array comparative genomic hybridization showed a 3.89 Mb de novo 14q24.1q24.2 deletion.

After the diagnosis he received ursodeoxycholic acid and prednisolone. Cholestasis and liver enzymes improved markedly after 1 month and remained improved one year after initial treatment, with lower serum copper and manganese and improved tremor, ataxia and pruritus. AMA-M2 was positive 4 months and negative 6 months after treatment.

repeated testing of circulating autoantibodies revealed that the patient was positive for AMA-M2 4 months after the treatment

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not date the AMA positivity to the time of diagnosis or treat the workup immunoblot as positive.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract says the patient presented with abnormal liver enzymes and pruritus "for more than 5 years"; the case text dates pruritus onset to after age 13 and the AST/ALP increases to age 3. The two statements are compatible (not a conflict), but the abstract duration is imprecise and its scope over the enzyme abnormality is unclear.

evidence.quote: presented with abnormal liver enzymes levels and pruritus for more than 5 years
after he turned 13 years old, he began to experience unexplained pruritus

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not compute an onset age from the abstract duration.

ambiguities.issue: The authors state the patient has not yet met the 2022 APASL diagnostic requirements for PBC with AIH features, yet describe the diagnosis as supported by interface hepatitis and treatment response; AIH features are kept provisional.

evidence.quote: Though our patient has not yet met the diagnostic requirements for PBC with AIH features according to the 2022 APASL guidance

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not treat AIH features as fully confirmed criteria-based overlap syndrome.

ambiguities.issue: ALP reference intervals differ: the text gives normal <122 U/L while Table 1 lists age-banded ranges (16–19 yr 58–237; ≥19 yr 28–94). Both are kept as printed; no flags were derived from either.

ambiguities.issue: Hedged exclusions (drug-induced liver injury "extremely low" likelihood, hepatocellular carcinoma "low possibility") are not explicit exclusions and are recorded as possible differentials; the cause of hepatocerebral degeneration is hedged and not recorded.

evidence.quote: The likelihood of drug-induced liver injury appears to be extremely low
which may be caused by cholestasis- and liver cirrhosis-related manganese deposition

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not treat these as refuted conditions or asserted causes.

article_limitations: Table 1 cells marked NT (not tested) are not individual observations; 70 NT cells were not recorded as facts and appear only as missing cells in the measurement series.
